subject: Competitive bake-off recap: Redwood vs Atlas - ZenWell next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Mehta <sanjay@zenwell.health>, Priya Das <priya.das@zenwell.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed bake-off plan (Redwood vs Atlas)

Hi Sanjay / Priya -

Thanks again for taking the time today - really great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps for the competitive bake-off so you can share with the committee.

Key pain points you confirmed:
- High per-token inference costs and unpredictable bill spikes (esp. during sequence-heavy billing workflows).
- Latency variability on current Atlas endpoints causing poor user experience for interactive clinician workflows (~800-1200ms currently).
- Requirement for private deployment option and strict audit logs for PHI datasets.

Goals you outlined:
- Achieve sub-400ms median tail latency for 2k-token scenarios in production workloads.
- Reduce per-query cost by 30-40% vs Atlas with equivalent output quality.
- Validate Private (VPC) deployment + KMS integration for HIPAA controls.

Decision criteria (committee):
- Latency at scale (P95/P99),
- Cost per 1k tokens in expected mixed workload,
- Output quality on existing prompt set (accuracy + hallucination rate),
- Security/compliance posture (SOC 2, KMS/HSM, audit logs),
- Time to production + ops burden.

Proposed bake-off plan (timeline / tests):
1) POC environment: Redwood will provide a short-lived private endpoint + test token access (sandbox) within 5 business days.
2) Baseline workload: We'll run your representative workload (chat + batching mixed traffic) over a 24-hour window to capture P50/P95/P99 and cost.
3) Quality evaluation: Run the provided prompt set (you shared 120 prompts) and produce: automated scoring + 10 manual audits for hallucination/accuracy.
4) Failover & security validation: Demonstrate key rotation via KMS and provide audit log sample.

Next steps / asks from ZenWell:
- Please confirm the primary evaluation prompts (you mentioned the triage + discharge set) - reply with final list or the Drive link.
- Confirm names of decision-makers for the final demo (I have Sanjay, Priya, and Dr. Kim on my notes).
- Agree to the proposed 24-48 hour window for the live baseline run next week (preferred dates: May 25-26).

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-plan.pdf (12 KB) - includes test matrix and metrics we will collect.

I'll loop Marissa in for pricing/commit questions after you confirm the test window.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Hi Sanjay / Priya -

Great - thanks for the quick confirm. A few concrete items before the run next week: 

1) POC access: We'll provision a sandbox private endpoint and send test credentials by EOD May 21.
2) Data: We can run on your anonymized samples if you're comfortable; otherwise the prompt + synthetic context is fine for latency/cost baselines. For quality checks we prefer a small set of real anonymized examples (no PHI).
3) Ballpark savings: For the mixed chat + encoding workload you described, our conservative estimate is 25-40% lower per-query cost vs the Atlas configuration you shared. We'll provide exact numbers after the 24-hour run.
4) Private POC timeline: Typical turnaround to stand up a short-lived private sandbox with KMS configured is ~3-5 business days (we'll need a POA and brief network info).

Attached: ZenWell bake-off criteria spreadsheet (zenwell-bakeoff-criteria.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
- Confirm sample data approach (anonymized vs synthetic) - Sanjay to confirm.
- Redwood to provision sandbox credentials by May 21 - Jordan action.
- Run baseline May 25, share results by May 26 EOD - Redwood action.
- Marissa to follow up with pricing/commit options after baseline.

If that looks good I'll schedule the provisioning kickoff for May 21.

Best,
Jordan Blake
